texts.li: {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef}, as kindly as {B_pronoun} could manage, whether {A_pronoun} might keep downwind.
{B_nameDef} held {B_possessive} breath the moment {A_nameDef} came near, and made sure {A_nameDef} saw it.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that {A_possessive} kind can smell rot from across a room, and that {B_nameDef}'s bedroll needed burning.
{B_nameDef} talked with {A_nameDef} about the weather and the work as if it were the most ordinary thing in the world.
{B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} about the day {A_pronoun} came here, and looked {A_objective} in the face the whole time {A_pronoun} answered.
{A_nameDef} flinched when {B_nameDef} reached for {A_possessive} hand, and {B_nameDef} waited until {A_nameDef} gave it.
{B_nameDef} couldn't meet {A_nameDef}'s eyes, and said it felt like being read from the inside.
{A_nameDef} answered a question {B_nameDef} hadn't asked out loud, and {B_nameDef} took a step back.
Very politely, {B_nameDef} asked {A_nameDef} to stop whatever {A_pronoun} was doing, and {A_nameDef} said {A_pronoun} wasn't doing anything.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that every carved face in the colony was an obscenity and ought to be burned.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} argued over whether art has any place in a decent home, and neither gave ground.
{A_nameDef} told {B_nameDef} that anything fired from a distance is a coward's weapon, and that real glory is had close enough to smell the other fellow's breath.
With open contempt, {A_nameDef} wanted to know whether {B_nameDef} had ever once looked an enemy in the eye.
{A_nameDef} pointed out every weak spot in the colony's defenses to {B_nameDef}, and which ones {A_pronoun} meant to mend first.
{A_nameDef} taught {B_nameDef} where to stand in a doorway so that a whole raid has to come at you one at a time.
{A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} went over the colony's defenses point by point, as if the next raid were already on its way.
